svg.text: Regional Supernet Allocation & Hub-Spoke Subnet Sizing
Azure Virtual Network Manager (AVNM) Regional IPAM Supernet: 10.64.0.0/14 (262,144 IPv4)
ER + S2S VPN coexist; no NSG
90% of /20 preserved for NVA transit subnets and future gateway scale
Why /24 Hubs Fail: Four /26 platform subnets consume all 256 IPs (5 reserved/subnet),
leaving zero room for RouteServerSubnet (/26) or DNS Private Resolver (/28 to /24).
Optional Dual-Stack Edge Rule: Exact /64 IPv6 per subnet (fd00:db8:64:10::/64)
Every VM NIC still requires a primary IPv4 config; keep IPv6 out of VNets hosting
PostgreSQL Flexible VNet injection, Azure Firewall, Route Server, or DNS Resolver.
Azure VMware Solution (AVS) Private Cloud: 10.67.0.0/22 (min /22 per cloud)
Segmented automatically into NSX-T, vMotion, vSAN, and management subnets outside VNets;
must never overlap on-premises, Hub/Spoke RFC 1918, or AKS 100.64.0.0/16 address space.
Azure Networking Field Architect Handbook | Architecture Reference
